title: Safe Reversing & Blind Spot Awareness
description: Learn defensive reversing procedures, blind zone clearance management, and high-visibility spotter protocols when pedestrians are in quarry loading areas.
trigger_reason: Recommended after a high-risk rear proximity event.
key_takeaways: Always sound two horn blasts prior to reversing in low visibility conditions.
Maintain a 7-meter dynamic exclusion perimeter behind active machines.
Bring machine to complete stop before attempting camera or mirror verification.

quiz.question: When reversing in wet conditions with visibility below 200m, what is the mandatory immediate action when a proximity alert sounds?
options: Accelerate past the hazard area quickly to clear the lane.
Stop machine safely, engage neutral lock, and verify the rear zone before proceeding.
Mute the alert and continue at 10 km/h.
Sound continuous horn while continuing to reverse.
quiz.explanation: Immediately stopping the machine eliminates kinetic risk and allows safe visual confirmation of blind spot clearance.

title: Efficient Idle Management
description: Techniques for minimizing unnecessary engine idling during haul truck staging delays to cut diesel emissions and avoid DPF filter soot loading.
trigger_reason: Recommended because idle time exceeded your typical range.
key_takeaways: Engage auto-idle mode (800 RPM) if wait time exceeds 3 minutes.
Shut down engine if wait time exceeds 6 minutes.
Avoid high-idle power mode when waiting for truck positioning.

quiz.question: What is the recommended protocol if you are waiting for a haul truck for longer than 3 minutes?
options: Keep engine revving at 2000 RPM to stay warm.
Throttle down to low idle (800 RPM) or engage auto-idle feature.
Turn off cab air conditioning only.
Begin dry digging without a haul truck.
quiz.explanation: Switching to low idle saves up to 4 litres of diesel per hour and protects emission filters from particulate build-up.

title: Steep Slope & Incline Handling
description: Best practices for operating excavators and loaders on 10°-15° inclines while managing hydraulic oil temperatures and center-of-gravity stability.
trigger_reason: Precautionary module for upcoming 14° excavation zone.
key_takeaways: Keep heavy loads low to the terrain when climbing or descending slopes.
Never turn across slopes steeper than 10 degrees.
Monitor hydraulic oil temp under high incline relief valve pressures.

quiz.question: Why does operating on a 12° slope increase machine fuel consumption even with standard digging cycles?
options: The operator is pressing the pedal too hard.
Hydraulic pumps experience continuous backpressure and slew motors work against gravity slope resistance.
Fuel evaporates faster at higher elevation.
Tracks slip 100% of the time on slopes.
quiz.explanation: Gravity resistance against machine weight and hydraulic slew motors creates unavoidable continuous hydraulic load on steep inclines.
